item.text: {"text":"Recent work distinguishes temporal interest, factual support, and preference alignment. [HyperHawkes (WWW 2025)](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/) models recurring intents and their temporal dynamics; repeated related interactions can support a recurring-interest hypothesis, but do not establish ownership or a satisfied need. [Beyond Factual Correctness (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03080) shows that factually grounded recommendation explanations can still conflict with user preferences, motivating feature-level evaluation. [Beyond Facts (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06539) decomposes expressed intent into individually checkable constraints. Together, these suggest separating recent repeated interest, apparent duplication, and explicit compatibility conflict instead of treating all rejection explanations as equivalent.\n\nFor this task, a practical adaptation is an evidence ledger: each diagnostic claim records history item IDs, timestamps, exact title/description spans, candidate spans, and a supported/contradicted/unknown judgment. Repeated descriptive features across recent interactions support interest continuity; similar products indicate possible redundancy, not proof that another is unnecessary. Compatibility rejection requires an explicit conflicting specification and evidence linking the relevant requirement to the history; missing specifications warrant abstention. [Sufficient Context (ICLR 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.06037) supports evaluating evidence sufficiency separately from answer confidence and using it to guide abstention. Manually audit the twenty training users—five per category—with a fixed rubric, ideally independent annotation and adjudication; measure supported-claim precision, unsupported-conflict rate, abstention coverage, and reviewer agreement. This is a proposed calibration protocol, not a published result or evidence of actual user rejection. Keep simulated feedback distinct from observed human feedback, exclude unobserved traits and purchase readiness, and retain macro validation HR@10 as the selection criterion."}
